title: Model Landscape Differential Mapping and Decision Workbench
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Create a repeatable, quantitative workbench and decision playbook to map model-level differentials across latency, cost-per-token, quality delta (by eval cohorts), and operational risk. The output is a ranked set of procurement / fallback triggers with automated suggested mitigations (quantization profile, batching policy, or regional routing).

Background & Motivation:
Our current model scouting artifacts catalog raw signals (latency, cost, qualitative notes) but lack a standardized differential view relative to active production models and SKU-level economics. Sales and Platform teams ask for an actionable artifact: for a given customer workload profile, which model switches are acceptable, which require canarying, and what compensating actions (e.g., increase batch target, pin kv-cache policy) preserve SLA and unit economics?

Scope:
- In scope: open models and verified vendor-hosted variants that we actively consider for fallback or procurement.
- Out of scope: long-tail academic releases (unless flagged by Research).

Deliverables:
1) Model Differential Matrix CSV and an interactive notebook that computes per-workload deltas (latency, 95p; cost per 1k tokens; eval-quality delta for 3 canonical cohorts).
2) Decision Workbench UI spec (Figma + confluence) describing decision knobs, scoring weights, and exportable trigger rules for Ops.
3) Playbook: procurement triggers + mitigation runbook (quantization suggestion, required canary size, suggested rollout policy).
4) One pilot run comparing 3 candidate fallback models against a production conversational workload; results uploaded to the inference observability dashboard.

Acceptance criteria:
- Notebook ingests telemetry export and model bench CSV and outputs ranked triggers with rationale (human readable).
- Playbook includes at least 6 mitigation templates (e.g., apply 4-bit quant profile B, change autoscale burst to 150%, run 1% canary for 48h).
- Design spec reviewed and approved by Design and Eng leads.
- Pilot run results show no >5% increase in P99 latency when fallback is applied with recommended mitigations.

Success metrics:
- Time to produce procurement recommendation reduced from ~2 weeks to <3 days.
- Ops accepts at least 2 automated trigger rules into the staging policy engine.

Method & approach:
1) Define canonical workload profiles (chat-short, chat-long, embeddings-bulk) and mapping rules for token distribution.
2) Use historical telemetry from Console (token mix, p50/p95/p99 latency, failure rates) as baseline.
3) Compute delta vectors between candidate models and baseline for each workload profile.
4) Score differentials with configurable weights: latency sensitivity, cost elasticity, quality tolerance.
5) Translate top-ranked differentials into concrete trigger rules (priority, canary size, mitigation template).

Data sources & artifacts referenced:
- Telemetry export: Console > Exports > model_telemetry_2026Q1.csv
- Benchmarks: s3://redwood-bench/model-bench/2026-02/
- Canonical eval sets: gdrive://redwood-drive/pm/canonical-evals/2026/

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: eval-quality deltas are noisy for small cohorts. Mitigation: bootstrap with synthetic augmentations and conservatively widen confidence intervals.
- Risk: telemetry gaps for new hosted vendors. Mitigation: require synthetic microbench harness for any model considered in this workbench.

Timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (2026-02-20 to 2026-02-26): define workloads, data contract for telemetry, sketch notebook inputs.
- Week 2: implement notebook + initial diff matrix.
- Week 3: design decision workbench UI + playbook draft.
- Week 4: pilot run + consolidate artifacts + handoff to Ops for policy staging.

Next steps (today):

- Create starter notebook repo and seed with sample CSVs.
- Schedule 1-hour alignment with Design and Research (invite sent).
